original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: On the selected #1094 gauge44 provider, census size-16 diagonal rank-16 batches drawn only from uninterrupted rank-one child runs on distinct destination columns, in both orientations; price the exact transformed local profile with all additional interface costs optimistically set to zero.
scope_change_reason: The broad rank-shape card is refined away from the heavily covered same-column frame-retiming and eight-term masked-decoder families. This changes the child interface: one rank-16 diagonal block child serves sixteen rank-one children across distinct output columns. The bounded experiment stops if even the zero-additional-cost profile misses the 5% ceiling gate.
bottleneck_link: Rank-one children are a large share of the selected local recursive mass. A rank-16 child can lower the moment per unit of preserved rank mass, so a valid cross-column batch could improve the binding complex-side ceiling.
stop_rule: Restrict to non-overlapping size-16 batches wholly contained in uninterrupted rank-one climb runs in the hash-pinned selected provider, ignoring only explicit phase markers. Grant all new copying, source, frame, interface, hosting, output-storage, precision and restoration costs zero for the ceiling screen. Stop without physical rewriting if the resulting exact ceiling is below 1.05 times the selected local-word ceiling; do not expand into nonconsecutive buffering or a different word in this cycle.
evidence: Both source orientations have 2,412 rank-one climbs and exactly eight admissible size-16 batches, serving 128 climbs. The mass-preserving ideal profile {1:2284, 2:418, 3:432, 4:142, 5:82, 8:8, 16:8} has exact rational ceiling upper endpoint 1719107428154/10^15, 1.7191% above the baseline 1690054109089/10^15 and below the 5% target. The 16-way diagonal block identity is exact. Every additional physical interface charge is waived in this favorable screen; no physical admission, new supplier, or kappa is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can nonconsecutive rank-one children be buffered into diagonal rank-16 batches with a fully charged source, copy, frame, hosting, output, and arbitrary-dirty restoration schedule?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The eight contiguous batches cover too little rank-one payload to pass the 5% ceiling screen; a larger packing would be needed before the new interface could affect the binding supplier materially.
open_questions.first_step: Pin operand-ready/use windows from the selected local word, then solve a disjoint 16-way interval packing problem and price one emitted batch end to end.
open_questions.blocked_by: The pinned local event trace records columns and frame changes but does not specify a multi-column dirty-state memory layout, operand lifetimes, or the restoration contract for an M16 child.
